messages.author: 7ddd2c1b6d8a27ef
messages.subject: Left justification of axis text
parts:
I am trying to make a dotplot. I have about 60 points, each with a longish descriptive label so I'd like to print the labels along the y-axis and plot the value along the x-axis. The problem comes when I want to left-justify the axis text as in the following example (with just two points).

test.dat <-
data.frame(desc=c("A very long name", "Another very long name"),
value=c(2,3))

qplot(x=value, y=desc, data=test.dat) + opts(axis.text.y=theme_text(hjust=0))

When I do this, the labels are indeed left-justified but they start at the y-axis and so disappear under the graph. If I keep them right-justified (hjust=1, the default), I can see them fine but they are not as easy to read.

Is there a way of using axis.text.y so I can left-justify the labels starting far away enough from the axis that they can be seen? Or do I have to add a text geom, which would I assume would give me finer-grain control? Or is there some other way? Thanks.

I am using ggplot2 0.8.6 and R 2.10.1. Thanks.

Jeff
